sources.authors: R. Weiner, B. A. Schmitt, H. Podhaisky
sources.title: Parallel Peer two-step W-methods and their application to MOL-systems

claims: Two-step methods propagate multiple peer variables of comparable order.
The fully parallel subclass removes current-step lower-triangular peer coupling so every current peer stage depends only on previous-step peer data.
Common-shift variants use one shifted matrix I-h*gamma*T_n and multiple independent right-hand sides.
Published theory includes order s-1 convergence/stability for general step sequences; stronger order/stability conditions are table-specific.
findings.consequence: Distinct GLM/peer plugin, not a reordering of RODAS5P. Must ship peer history, variable-step coefficients, startup, estimator, rejection/restart and output semantics.
limits: Family theorem does not certify a chosen coefficient table or adapter.
Need exact coefficient and step-ratio hypotheses.

sources.authors: B. A. Schmitt, R. Weiner, H. Podhaisky
sources.title: Multi-Implicit Peer Two-Step W-Methods for Parallel Time Integration

claims: Different implicit parameters/shifts may be assigned to different stages.
Current stages use only previous-step peer information and are independent.
Reported general subclass has order s-1, improved stiff damping and shared-memory matrix-free Krylov experiments.
findings.consequence: Compare independent shifted Krylov solves against shared-basis/multi-shift Krylov only after proving that the exact operator/shift contract permits reuse.
limits: Different shifts may need separate preconditioners/factorizations.
Concurrency may be offset by setup/storage/communication.

sources.title: Global error estimation and control in linearly-implicit parallel two-step peer W-methods
sources.venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 236(6), 1226-1239

claims: Method-matched local/global error estimation and adaptive step-size control exist for linearly implicit parallel two-step peer W methods.
Estimator equations are coupled to the exact method family and cannot be replaced by RODAS embedded weights or generic RK estimates.
findings.consequence: Recover the typeset estimator equations and exact coefficient conventions before implementation.
limits: Extracted PDF symbols may be lost; transcription needs independent check.

sources.title: Stabilized explicit peer methods with parallelism across the stages for stiff problems

claims: TASE-preconditioned explicit two-step peer formulas yield linearly implicit methods with independent current peer stages.
SEPP2 is reported strongly A-stable; SEPP3 has a reported A(theta) angle about 89.4 degrees and stiff-limit spectral radius about 0.69; SEPP4's reported angle is much narrower, about 32.62 degrees.
findings.negative_or_limit: The numerical examples report sequential implementations; this is not measured native stage-parallel speedup for a VigilODE adapter.
findings.consequence: SEPP2/3 are low-order candidate controls. SEPP4 is a weaker stiff-sector comparator unless a chosen application fits the sector. Count all TASE/preconditioner solves.
limits: Stability is coefficient and preconditioner specific.
Order/stage parallelism does not imply cost advantage.

sources.title: L(theta)-stable peer methods with reused stages for advection-diffusion-reaction problems

claims: Linearly implicit two-step peer methods are tailored to nonlinear advection-diffusion-reaction semi-discretizations.
Families include L-stable and L(theta)-stable methods with theta approaching 90 degrees.
Stage reuse lowers effective evaluations and linear-system/LU costs for selected order 3 and 4 designs.
findings.consequence: Mandatory modern MOL comparator. Inspect the selected tableau's current-step dependency graph before calling it stage-parallel; reuse alone is insufficient.
limits: Selected ADR workloads do not establish general performance.
VigilODE adapter and matched-error crossover are untested.

sources.title: Stiff Norm Estimates for Variable-Stepsize Peer Two-Step Methods

claims: Grid-independent norm estimates are derived for variable-step diagonally implicit L(alpha)-stable peer methods on stiff semilinear systems.
Constructed methods reach order five with stage order five and a superconvergent order-six result under stated assumptions.
The analysis emphasizes products of step-varying propagation matrices; fixed-grid spectral radius alone is insufficient for variable-step global stability.
findings.consequence: Use as a high-order variable-step stiff-norm comparator. Assume sequential diagonal-implicit stage dependency until a selected table proves independence.
limits: Preprint hypotheses and exact tables need independent audit.
Diagonal implicitness is not synonymous with stage parallelism.

selection.primary: Common-shift parallel two-step W/peer; PTSW2B is the first exact certificate but only order two.
selection.secondary: Multi-implicit peer-W or verified TASE-SEPP3, depending on exact table and cost.
selection.high_order_control: 2026 variable-step L(alpha)-stable order-five diagonally implicit peer; not presumed parallel.
selection.MOL_cost_control: 2026 L(theta)-stable reused-stage peer; stage DAG must be checked.
selection.nonstiff_parallel_control: EPPEER explicit peer family; DQC estimator restrictions remain method-specific.
selection.novelty_boundary: Parallel peer methods themselves are established prior art. Potential novelty must come from a newly derived/certified algorithmic combination, rollback/error guarantees, operator/geometry integration and matched achieved-error end-to-end evidence.

research_gates: Exact primary coefficient tables and exact-rational reconstruction.
Order, stage-order, preconsistency, zero-stability and variable-step domain.
Full complex sector/stiff-limit claims; numeric root locus remains NUMERICALLY_CHECKED, not PROVED.
Correct startup and peer history order.
Stage dependency graph and actual CPU concurrency.
Full-IVP achieved-error comparison including setup, startup, rejection, output and fallback.
